intro: All three say "not only A, but B", and the difference is what happens to A. ばかりか accepts A and piles a more surprising B on top, in the same direction. どころか rejects A: the truth is far beyond it or the opposite of it. はもちろん treats A as obvious and adds B as the extension.

skills.rule: A ばかりか B も / まで: not only A, but even B, with B going further in the same direction.
skills.explain:
ばかりか (and the more neutral ばかりでなく) follows a noun directly, or the plain form of a verb or adjective; な-adjectives keep な: 彼ばかりか, 遅刻したばかりか, 高いばかりか, 不便なばかりか. The second half adds something with も, まで or さえ that is more surprising or more serious than A: 財布ばかりか携帯までなくした.

A is true, and A and B point the same way: both good or both bad. If B contradicts A, you need どころか.

ばかりか reports facts, so the second half cannot be a request, an invitation, a command or a statement of your own intention. 水だけでなく食べ物も持ってきてください is correct; with ばかりか it is wrong. In those cases use だけでなく or はもちろん (ばかりでなく is also acceptable there).
patterns: [noun] ばかりか [noun] も / まで [predicate]
[plain verb / い-adj / な-adj + な] ばかりか、[more] も [predicate]

examples.jp: 兄[あに]{ばかりか}、弟[おとうと]まで風邪[かぜ]をひいた。
examples.en: Not only my older brother but even my younger brother caught a cold.

examples.jp: この部屋[へや]は狭[せま]い{ばかりか}、駅[えき]からも遠[とお]い。
examples.en: This room is not only small; it's also far from the station.

examples.jp: 彼女[かのじょ]は英語[えいご]{ばかりか}、中国語[ちゅうごくご]も話[はな]せる。
examples.en: She can speak not only English but Chinese as well.

examples.jp: 財布[さいふ]{ばかりか}、パスポートまでなくしてしまった。
examples.en: I lost not only my wallet but even my passport.

examples.jp: その店[みせ]は値段[ねだん]が安[やす]い{ばかりか}、味[あじ]もいい。
examples.en: That restaurant is not only cheap; the food is good too.

examples.jp: 熱[ねつ]が下[さ]がらない{ばかりか}、咳[せき]まで出[で]てきた。
examples.en: Not only has my fever not gone down, I've even started coughing.

contrast.note: どころか rejects A: 痩せるどころか太った (far from losing weight, I gained). ばかりか keeps A as true and adds B in the same direction.
だけでなく is the neutral everyday form and can lead into a request or intention: 名前だけでなく住所も書いてください. ばかりか cannot.
はもちろん says A is obvious and B is the extension. ばかりか stresses that B is surprising.

mistakes.bad: 水[みず]{ばかりか}、食[た]べ物[もの]も持[も]ってきてください。
mistakes.good: 水[みず]{だけでなく}、食[た]べ物[もの]も持[も]ってきてください。
mistakes.note: ばかりか cannot end in a request; use だけでなく.

mistakes.bad: 雨[あめ]がやむ{ばかりか}、もっと強[つよ]くなった。
mistakes.good: 雨[あめ]がやむ{どころか}、もっと強[つよ]くなった。
mistakes.note: The rain did not stop at all, so A is rejected: どころか.

mistakes.bad: この町[まち]は静[しず]か{ばかりか}、緑[みどり]も多[おお]い。
mistakes.good: この町[まち]は静[しず]かな{ばかりか}、緑[みどり]も多[おお]い。
mistakes.note: A な-adjective keeps な before ばかりか.

skills.tip: A is true, B goes further the same way, and the sentence is a plain statement: ばかりか.

skills.rule: A どころか B: far from A, the truth is B. A is rejected as wrong, or as far too small.
skills.explain:
どころか follows a noun or the plain form of a verb or adjective, and it throws A away. It has three uses.

Reversal: B is the opposite of A, often of what was expected or hoped: 痩せるどころか三キロ太った (far from losing weight, I put on three kilos); 謝るどころか怒り出した. Here ばかりか is impossible, because A did not happen.

Not even: A is a high bar, and B, a much more basic thing, also fails, so B is negative with も or さえ: 漢字どころか、ひらがなも読めない (kanji? I can't even read hiragana). The easier thing goes second.

Understatement: A is a modest figure and the truth is far bigger, with も: 一時間どころか三時間も待った (not one hour: three whole hours). Unlike ばかりか, A is denied, not kept.

It also works as a reply that rejects the other person's word: 暇どころか、寝る時間もない (free? I don't even have time to sleep).
patterns: [harder thing] どころか [easier thing] も / さえ [negative]

examples.jp: 暇[ひま]{どころか}、寝[ね]る時間[じかん]もありません。
examples.en: Free? Far from it: I don't even have time to sleep.

examples.jp: 漢字[かんじ]{どころか}、ひらがなもまだ読[よ]めません。
examples.en: Forget kanji: I can't even read hiragana yet.

examples.jp: ダイエットを始[はじ]めたのに、痩[や]せる{どころか}太[ふと]ってしまった。
examples.en: I started a diet, but far from losing weight, I gained.

examples.jp: 薬[くすり]を飲[の]んだら、よくなる{どころか}、もっと悪[わる]くなった。
examples.en: After taking the medicine, far from getting better, I got worse.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は謝[あやま]る{どころか}、怒[おこ]り出[だ]した。
examples.en: Far from apologising, he started getting angry.

examples.jp: 貯金[ちょきん]{どころか}、毎月[まいつき]借金[しゃっきん]が増[ふ]えている。
examples.en: Far from saving, I'm getting deeper into debt every month.

contrast.note: ばかりか keeps A and adds more in the same direction: 狭いばかりか遠い. どころか denies A: 広いどころか、ベッドも入らない.
はもちろん affirms A as obvious. どころか says A is not even close to the truth.
だけでなく just adds B to A. It never denies A, so it cannot express "far from".

mistakes.bad: 痩[や]せる{ばかりか}、太[ふと]ってしまった。
mistakes.good: 痩[や]せる{どころか}、太[ふと]ってしまった。
mistakes.note: Gaining weight contradicts losing it, so A is rejected: どころか.

mistakes.bad: 漢字[かんじ]{どころか}、ひらがなも読[よ]めます。
mistakes.good: 漢字[かんじ]{どころか}、ひらがなも読[よ]めません。
mistakes.note: In the "not even" pattern the easier thing comes second and the verb is negative.

skills.tip: If A turns out false ("far from it", "forget A", "not A but much more"), it is どころか. If A stays true, it is not.

skills.rule: A はもちろん B も: A goes without saying, and B too.
skills.explain:
はもちろん (formal: はもとより; emphatic: はもちろんのこと) follows a noun. It puts the obvious case first and adds a less obvious one with も: 週末はもちろん、平日も混んでいる (of course at weekends, and on weekdays too). Other particles can stay before は: 日本ではもちろん.

A is the case the statement most obviously fits, so the order depends on the predicate. With "can read", the easier thing is obvious: ひらがなはもちろん漢字も読める. With "can't read", the harder thing is: 漢字はもちろん、ひらがなも読めない (I can't read hiragana, let alone kanji).

Unlike ばかりか, the second half can be any kind of sentence, including requests: 名前はもちろん、住所も書いてください. Standing alone, もちろん is just the adverb "of course".
patterns: [obvious case] はもちろん、[extension] も [predicate]
[obvious case] はもちろん、[extension] も [request]

examples.jp: 週末[しゅうまつ]{はもちろん}、平日[へいじつ]も忙[いそが]しいです。
examples.en: I'm busy at weekends, of course, and on weekdays too.

examples.jp: この公園[こうえん]は子[こ]ども{はもちろん}、大人[おとな]も楽[たの]しめる。
examples.en: Children, of course, but adults too can enjoy this park.

examples.jp: 名前[なまえ]{はもちろん}、住所[じゅうしょ]も書[か]いてください。
examples.en: Please write your name, of course, and your address too.

examples.jp: この歌[うた]は日本[にほん]{はもちろん}、海外[かいがい]でも人気[にんき]がある。
examples.en: This song is popular in Japan, of course, and abroad as well.

examples.jp: 漢字[かんじ]{はもちろん}、ひらがなもまだ書[か]けません。
examples.en: I can't write hiragana yet, let alone kanji.

contrast.note: ばかりか stresses that B is surprising and cannot end in a request. はもちろん stresses that A is obvious and allows any ending.
どころか denies A. はもちろん affirms A as self-evident.
に限らず only says A is not the only case. はもちろん adds that A is the obvious one.

mistakes.bad: 漢字[かんじ]{はもちろん}、ひらがなも読[よ]めます。
mistakes.good: ひらがな{はもちろん}、漢字[かんじ]も読[よ]めます。
mistakes.note: With "can read", the obvious case is the easier one, so hiragana goes first.

mistakes.bad: 名前[なまえ]{ばかりか}、住所[じゅうしょ]も書[か]いてください。
mistakes.good: 名前[なまえ]{はもちろん}、住所[じゅうしょ]も書[か]いてください。
mistakes.note: A request after "not only" needs はもちろん or だけでなく, not ばかりか.

skills.tip: Put "obviously" in front of A. If that sounds right, はもちろん fits.
